title: Benchmarking Large Language Models in Code Generation: A Systematic Review
incompatible_concepts: Qualitative opinion surveys without code evaluation
unit_of_analysis: Peer-reviewed empirical studies of LLM code generation
epistemological_rationale: Statistical generalisability of benchmark performance across models requires a Positivist stance with quantitative evidence.

research_questions.text: What automated benchmarks are used in the literature to measure LLM code generation pass rates?
What is the measured performance difference between dense retrieval and graph-boosted RAG for code synthesis?
research_questions.required_evidence_type: Ablation delta tables and latency measurements

research_questions.text: What limitations and threats to validity are most commonly reported in LLM code generation benchmarking studies?
research_questions.required_evidence_type: Reported limitations and threats to validity

inclusion_criteria.criterion: Presents a novel computational model, prompt architecture, or RAG pipeline for code generation
Evaluates performance quantitatively against public standard benchmark datasets
Reports at least one limitation or threat to validity

exclusion_criteria.criterion: Position papers or non-peer-reviewed blog posts without empirical code evaluation
Studies focusing purely on natural language translation without code execution

matrix_dimensions.name: Model Architecture & Parameters
matrix_dimensions.description: Extract foundation model name and parameter size (e.g. Llama-3-70B, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-Coder).

matrix_dimensions.name: Benchmark Dataset(s)
matrix_dimensions.description: Extract specific test suites used (HumanEval, MBPP, SWE-bench, DS-1000).

matrix_dimensions.name: pass@1 / Execution Accuracy
matrix_dimensions.description: Extract numerical pass@1 or unit test pass percentages reported.

matrix_dimensions.description: Extract engineering constraints, compute requirements, or index latency.
